title: A CDC tip is to repeat bababa and then offer a real word
summary: The CDC 9-month tips say to repeat a baby's bababa and then say a word such as book.
body: A caregiver tip on the CDC 9-month page says to repeat the baby's sounds and then say simple words that use those sounds. The example is: if the baby says bababa, repeat bababa, then say book. That is a suggested activity, not a milestone the baby is scored on. The page does not claim the baby learns book from one repetition. It is one United States tip among others on that page.

sources.title: Milestones by 9 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Opened 2026-11-26. Reviewed date on the page is 16 May 2026. Supports the tip to repeat bababa and then say book.
